case_title: Prashant Bharti v. State of NCT of Delhi
evidence_type: Mobile phone call records, medical examination reports, statements under s.164 CrPC, investigating officer's chargesheet findings
trial_court_outcome: Charges framed under ss.328, 354 and 376 IPC on 1.12.2008; no verdict or sentence recorded
high_court_outcome: Accused's writ petition to quash FIR dismissed 27.8.2007; victim's writ petition dismissed; revision against framing of charges dismissed 16.1.2009
neutral_facts: The victim, aged 21, had known the accused for about four months. On 15.2.2007 the accused telephoned her at about 8.45 pm and asked her to meet him at Lodhi Colony, New Delhi. When she arrived he drove her around in his car and offered her a cold drink (Pepsi), which she said contained an intoxicating substance. She felt inebriated and alleged that the accused touched her breasts and continued to misbehave despite her objections. She got out of the car, took an auto-rickshaw home and complained to the police on 16.2.2007. A medical examination at AIIMS found no evidence of poisoning. The accused was arrested the same day. On 21.2.2007 the victim made a supplementary statement alleging that, on the assurance of marriage, the accused had physical relations with her at his house on 23.12.2006, 25.12.2006 and 1.1.2007. A medical examination on 21.2.2007 recorded that she had no external injuries and her hymen was not intact. No vaginal smear was taken because more than a month had elapsed, and her clothes were not sent for forensic examination because she had changed them. The police could not recover the drink container, glass or undergarments, and no blood sample was sent for analysis. Mobile phone call records showed that the accused was at Noida and Ghaziabad, including a function from 9.15 pm to 11.30 pm on 15.2.2007, and that no calls were made by him to the victim that day. Her call records placed her at other locations in Delhi and in conversation with friends. A tenancy verification affidavit described her as married. The victim's statement was recorded under section 164 CrPC on 27.2.2007.
offence_severity: Minimum 7 years for s.376 IPC (as stated in the High Court observation quoted in the judgment); maximum not stated
physical_harm: No external injuries; hymen not intact per AIIMS report; no evidence of poisoning; no death
key_evidence_accepted: Mobile phone call details placing the accused in Noida/Ghaziabad and the victim elsewhere on 15.2.2007; divorce judgment and marriage certificate showing the victim was married during the alleged occurrences; the AIIMS medical reports; the investigating officer's chargesheet acknowledging no proof was found
witness_credibility: The court found the victim's assertion of a promise of marriage falsified by her subsisting marriage, and her supplementary allegations and her description of herself as unmarried to police were found false
custody_duration: Arrested 16.2.2007; duration of custody not stated
bail_history: Bail granted by Additional Sessions Judge, Delhi on 12.3.2007
trial_duration: offence: 23.12.2006, 25.12.2006, 1.1.2007 and 15.2.2007 (alleged); trial judgment: not given (charges framed 1.12.2008); High Court: 27.8.2007 and 16.1.2009; Supreme Court: 23.1.2013
legal_representation: Appellant: K.T.S. Tulsi, Gaurave Bhargava (for Niraj Gupta). Respondent State: R.K. Rathore, Vikas Bansal, D.S. Mahra (for Anil Katiyar), appearing with the complainant
investigation_status: FIR registered 16.2.2007; chargesheet filed 28.6.2007; investigation yielded no positive result; charges framed 1.12.2008
procedural_irregularity: Medical examination delayed to 21.2.2007, so no vaginal smear or forensic testing of clothes; chargesheet based only on the s.164 statement
appeal_history: Trial court: charges framed 1.12.2008 (no verdict). High Court: writ petitions dismissed 27.8.2007 and later; revision dismissed 16.1.2009. Supreme Court: appeal allowed; FIR, chargesheet and framing of charges quashed
prosecution_argument: Not stated; the judgment records that the complainant filed no pleadings and did not refute the accused's material
defence_argument: The accused was not at the place of occurrence; his affidavit and mobile records showed he was at Noida and Ghaziabad; the allegations were false and he was falsely implicated
legal_principle_applied: Four-step test for quashing under s.482 CrPC from Rajiv Thapar: whether defence material is sound and indubitable, rules out the allegations, is unrefuted, and whether trial would be an abuse of process
precedent_relied_upon: Gajraj v. State (NCT) of Delhi (2011) 12 SCR 701 = (2011) 10 SCC 675; Rajiv Thapar & Ors. v. Madan Lal Kapoor [2013] 1 SCR
other_sentence_order: FIR No. 47 of 2007, the chargesheet dated 28.6.2007 and the framing of charges on 1.12.2008 quashed
